aliases: equivalence relation on arrows compatible with composition

evidence.intree_statement: Class HomCongruence {C : Category} (R : HomRel C) : Type := { cong_incl {x y}{f g : x ~> y} : f ≈ g → R x y f g; cong_sym : R x y f g → R x y g f; cong_trans : R x y f g → R x y g h → R x y f h; cong_comp {x y z}{f f' : y ~> z}{g g' : x ~> y} : R y z f f' → R x y g g' → R x z (f ∘ g) (f' ∘ g') }  (HomRel C := ∀ x y : C, (x ~> y) → (x ~> y) → Prop)
Lemma cong_refl ... {x y}(f : x ~> y) : R x y f f  (reflexivity derived from cong_incl of ≈), giving Quotient_equivalence : Equivalence (R x y).

statement_record.book: A congruence on a category C is an equivalence relation f ~ g on arrows with (1) f~g implies dom(f)=dom(g), cod(f)=cod(g), and (2) f~g implies b.f.a ~ b.g.a for all pre/post-composable a,b.
statement_record.intree: HomCongruence R: R is a Prop-valued relation on parallel homs (x~>y), containing ≈ (cong_incl), symmetric (cong_sym), transitive (cong_trans), and closed under two-sided composition (cong_comp: R f f' → R g g' → R (f∘g)(f'∘g')).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same (faithful setoid rephrasing). The typing R x y : (x~>y)→(x~>y)→Prop makes Awodey's condition (1) automatic (only parallel arrows are related). cong_comp is the full two-sided composition compatibility of condition (2). Difference: the in-tree class additionally requires ≈ ⊆ R (cong_incl) instead of plain-equality reflexivity — this is the necessary setoid-library rephrasing (a congruence must respect the ambient hom-equivalence to descend), not a genuine strengthening; reflexivity is recovered from it.

evidence.intree_statement: Context (F : C ⟶ D)(HF : ∀ x y (f g : x ~> y), R x y f g → fmap[F] f ≈ fmap[F] g). Definition QuotientLift : Quotient C R ⟶ D := Build_Functor (Quotient C R) D (fun x => F x)(fun x y f => fmap[F] f) HF ...  — a functor identifying R-related morphisms lifts through the quotient.
Lemma QuotientLift_proj (f : x ~> y) : fmap[QuotientLift] (fmap[QuotientProj] f) = fmap[F] f. Proof. reflexivity. Qed.  (factorization F = QuotientLift ∘ QuotientProj, definitional)

Lemma QuotientLift_unique (G : Quotient C R ⟶ D)(Hobj : ∀ x, fobj[G] x = fobj[F] x)(HG : ∀ x y f, hom_cast (Hobj x)(Hobj y)(fmap[G](fmap[QuotientProj] f)) ≈ fmap[F] f) : ∀ x y f, hom_cast (Hobj x)(Hobj y)(fmap[G] f) ≈ fmap[QuotientLift] f.

statement_record.book: Every functor F : C → D has a kernel category ker(F) determined by a congruence ~_F; and for any congruence ~ on C, (f~g ⟹ f~_F g) iff there is a factorization F~ : C/~ → D with F~ ∘ π = F.
statement_record.intree: Given a congruence R on C and a functor F with R x y f g → fmap F f ≈ fmap F g (i.e. R ⊆ ker F), QuotientLift : C/R → D satisfies QuotientLift ∘ QuotientProj = F (QuotientLift_proj) and is unique (QuotientLift_unique).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the operative content — the universal property that a functor killing the congruence factors uniquely through the quotient — is fully present (existence via QuotientLift, factorization via QuotientLift_proj, uniqueness via QuotientLift_unique). The hypothesis 'R x y f g → fmap F f ≈ fmap F g' IS exactly 'R refines ker F'. What is NOT packaged: the kernel congruence ~_F as a named object (ABSENT), the kernel category ker(F) (ABSENT), and the explicit biconditional (only the direction 'R ⊆ ker F ⟹ ∃! factorization' is stated; the trivial converse 'factorization exists ⟹ R ⊆ ker F' is not).

gap: The quotient universal property (existence + factorization + uniqueness of the lift) is present as QuotientLift / QuotientLift_proj / QuotientLift_unique for an arbitrary congruence R with R ⊆ ker F. evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Free : Category := {| obj := C; hom := tlist hom; homset _ _ := {| equiv := eq |}; id _ := tnil; compose _ _ _ f g := g +++ f |}  — the free/path category on the underlying quiver of C (vertices = objects, morphisms = finite composable paths).
Free ⊣ Forgetful over StrictCat: UniversalArrowQuiverCat / FreeForgetfulAdjunction package the universal property of the free category on a quiver (the relation-free case of a presentation).
Quotient C R : Category — the quotient of a category by an arbitrary hom-congruence R (the relation-imposing half of a presentation).

statement_record.book: From the free category C(G) on a finite graph G and a finite set Σ of path relations, form the least congruence ~_Σ identifying the two sides of each relation; C(G,Σ) := C(G)/~_Σ, with a UMP: any type-G diagram h : G → |D| respecting Σ extends uniquely to h̄ : C(G,Σ) → D.
statement_record.intree: The two halves exist as reusable kits: Free (path category on a quiver) with its free-forgetful adjunction over StrictCat, and Quotient (quotient of a category by a hom-congruence) with its lifting UMP. There is no in-tree assembly forming the least congruence generated by a finite relation set, nor a packaged C(G,Σ) with its combined UMP.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the free-category half and the quotient-by-a-congruence half are each present with their universal properties, but they are not composed into a finitely-presented-category construction; crucially the least congruence ~_Σ GENERATED by a set of relations (Awodey's 'intersection of all congruences containing the relations') is not constructed for general categories. The analogous full presentation machinery exists only one level down, for PROPs (Construction/PROP/Presentation.v), not for general categories.
